evidence.reason: At the pinned tip, run_command starts the child with start_new_session=True but calls _kill_process_group only in the TimeoutExpired and BaseException handlers. When communicate() returns normally, including for a nonzero returncode, execution proceeds directly to the returncode check or return without signaling or reaping the process group. A background descendant with redirected streams can therefore survive the exited command and still write under the checkout while a retry or lock release proceeds. The ordinary fix is to finalize the process group after normal communicate() completion, before checking returncode/returning, while preserving the existing timeout cleanup.
